result.topic_en: Riemann rewrites the one-dimensional isentropic gas equations (with $p=a^2\rho$) in terms of the Riemann invariants $p$ and $q$, writes their characteristic forms, sketches compactly supported initial data, and uses $p,q$ as independent variables (hodograph method) to reach a linear second-order equation for an auxiliary function $w$.

Definition of the Riemann invariants p, q
Velocity expressed through the Riemann invariants
Characteristic (transport) equations for the Riemann invariants

methods.what: Differentials of p, q along characteristic directions
Initial data with compact support for the invariants
Hodograph transformation: p and q taken as independent variables
Introduction of a potential w whose differential is an exact form in dp, dq
Linear second-order hyperbolic equation for w in the hodograph plane
